newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka says crushing rebels precursor to peace.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka says crushing rebels precursor to peace.

text.p: Sri Lankan President Chandrika Kumaratunga has emphasised the need to neutralise Tamil Tiger rebels militarily before finding a political solution to the country's ethnic crisis, newspapers reported on Monday.

The state-owned Daily News quoted Kumaratunga as saying at a commissioning parade of new army officers at the weekend that the government had no choice but to crush the separatists militarily as a precursor to a political solution.

"Our enemy is an intransigent minority professing to be the sole representative of a section of our population. Through armed action it prevents the acceptance of a reasonable solution to the most serious problem faced by the nation," the newspaper quoted her as saying.
"We have little choice except fighting this rebel group militarily."
The Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) have been fighting government troops for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in Sri Lanka's north and east since 1983.
The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the war. The LTTE say the toll is higher.

Some 20,000 troops launched a major offensive against LTTE through the northern Wanni brush jungle last month in an attempt to open a key northern highway to Jaffna peninsula, which was earlier the rebel stronghold.
The troops captured key rebel towns in the Wanni region before the rebels counter-attacked earlier this month. Casualties have been heavy on both sides.
The Defence Ministry says the operation against the rebels is continuing, but no major battles have been reported in the past two weeks.
